title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers, routing rules, and payload limits for openai-compat/tool-calls
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent regressions in streaming throughput and increased 504s for OpenAI-compat streaming routes under spike traffic, particularly when tool/function-calling payloads included large structured outputs. This PR adjusts streaming proxy buffer sizes, tightens routing rules to prefer local region dedicated capacity for low-latency tiers, and enforces conservative payload size limits and graceful truncation semantics for openai-compat tool calls.

What this change does: 1) Streaming proxy buffer tuning: increase default proxy_read buffer from 8KB to 64KB and add adaptive high-water marks to reduce upstream backpressure and burst-related stalls. Introduce PROXY_STREAM_MAX_CHUNK_MS to coalesce small chunks for low-throughput clients. 2) Routing rules: add route policy prioritization so requests with header x-rw-client-tier: low-latency hit dedicated pools in-region first, with fast fallback to hosted variants; reduce cross-region routing for streaming endpoints by default. 3) Payload limits and structured output: introduce configurable per-route payload_soft_limit (default 256KB) and payload_hard_limit (default 1MB) for OpenAI-compat endpoints. When soft limit exceeded, server emits structured partial response with metadata truncated=true and a resume_token where applicable; when hard limit exceeded, return 413 with clear error and guidance. 4) Tool/function calling stability: ensure function-call payloads are validated pre-forward and large tool responses are chunked and queued to the streaming proxy correctly; add a server-side sanitizer to strip overly large examples and avoid KV-cache amplification.

Compatibility and config: All new knobs are feature-flagged behind ff_api_gateway_streaming_buffer_tuning and ff_openai_compat_payload_limits. Defaults are conservative to avoid customer-facing regressions. Ops can tune per-tenant via route config in Redwood Console.

Testing and validation: Local stress suite (benchmark-lab) replayed production traces; synthetic spike test with 1000 concurrent streaming clients shows 40% reduction in transient 504s and 25% lower average time-to-first-byte for low-latency Tier requests. Integration tests were added for chunk coalescing, resume_token behavior, and function-call truncation. CI initially flaked on an unrelated unit test (streaming timeout race) and was rerun.

Rollout plan: Gradual rollout by region and tier over 2 weeks with canary traffic at 1%/5%/25%/100%; monitoring dashboards and alerts added (streaming-504-rate, stream-ttfb, openai-compat-truncation-rate). In case of regression rollback path is a single config toggle to disable ff_api_gateway_streaming_buffer_tuning.

review_conversation:
Samir: Can we back out the buffer increase for small clients — some mobile clients experience memory pressure?
Asha: Added adaptive high-water mark and PROXY_STREAM_MAX_CHUNK_MS to prevent unbounded growth; default keeps per-connection footprint low.
Elena: The routing priority change could cause capacity hotspots on Dedicated pools. Suggest a soft-limit for number of routed streams per pool.
Asha: Implemented soft connection cap and fallback policy; added metrics to alert on pool saturation.
Jonah: How does this interact with existing KV cache behavior? Could truncation break deterministic replay?
Asha: We added a truncation metadata flag and resume_token to maintain determinism; KV cache keys include resume_token when partial responses are used.
Samir: Request to add a migration note for console route config schema.
Asha: Added docs and console editor change.
Elena: Approve after CI green and integration tests added.
Jonah: Approve.
Status: CI passed on rerun, merged via squash. Merge SHA: 0f9e1d3b6c4a2b7e8d9f0a1b2c3d4e5f
release_notes:
- Improved streaming stability: tuned proxy buffers and added adaptive coalescing to reduce transient 504s.
- Routing: region-affinity and priority routing for low-latency tier; soft connection caps to avoid Dedicated hotspots.
- OpenAI-compat: configurable payload_soft_limit/payload_hard_limit with graceful truncation and resume_token support.
- Tool calls: pre-validation and chunking to improve streaming tool stability.
Notes: Feature-flagged; ops can roll back via ff_api_gateway_streaming_buffer_tuning toggle.
